subject: Public‑facing short blurb: data routing, subprocessors, and DPA alignment
content:
From: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Susan Park <susan@brightgate.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick public blurb request: routing/subprocessors and DPA alignment

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Acme has a final gating item before legal signs — we need a 2–3 sentence, customer‑facing paragraph that explains: how data is routed geographically (hosted API), whether customer data is shared with subprocessors, and reassurance that the DPA covers those subprocessors and cross‑border transfers. This will be pasted into our SOW appendix.

Susan (cc) will review for legal language. If you can include a one‑line link to your subprocessor list and call out any EU data routing controls, that would be ideal.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — EOD Wed would be fantastic.

Best,
Jared Liao
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corporation

Thanks Jared — looping in Laura and Kim to draft a customer‑friendly blurb and confirm DPA mapping. Rishi, can you confirm whether this needs any sales nuance (discounts/credits) or if we should keep it purely legal/product?

Proposal: keep the text short and non‑legal (for procurement/SOW) and attach our public subprocessor CSV + a DPA reference link. If possible, avoid any mention of specific cloud vendors in the blurb — point to the subprocessor list instead.

I attached a rough starter and the current subprocessor snapshot for Q1 so Laura/Kim can iterate.

Thanks — Mina

Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Susan Park <susan@brightgate.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick public blurb request: routing/subprocessors and DPA alignment

Drafted a short, plain‑language blurb below — aiming for simple Procurement copy that maps to our DPA without sounding like a legal excerpt. Treat as public‑facing text suitable for an SOW appendix.

——–
Redwood Inference routes API requests to regional hosting endpoints closest to the customer to minimize latency. We may transfer or route data across regions to provide the service and for availability; our DPA outlines the safeguards we apply to cross‑border transfers. We use a limited set of subprocessors to operate and maintain the hosted platform; a current list is posted here (link). All subprocessors are covered by contractual commitments consistent with the DPA and undergo security review.
——–

Kim — can you confirm that "covered by contractual commitments consistent with the DPA" is sufficient for Acme or if we should reference standard SCCs or specific transfer mechanisms?

Also attached a marked‑up DPA excerpt that shows the relevant clauses. I kept it intentionally non‑specific so it can live on the public console copy.

—Laura
Director, Product Marketing

Attachments: draft_dpa_v3.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick public blurb request: routing/subprocessors and DPA alignment

Laura — thanks, this reads well for procurement. A couple of legal clarifications I made inline and a suggested one‑sentence addendum for customers in the EU: we rely on legally recognized transfer mechanisms where required (e.g., SCCs or adequacy decisions) and we will make the specific mechanism available on request to contract signatories.

If you want the safest, most procurement‑friendly line: "Subprocessors are bound by our DPA and onward transfer mechanisms; specific transfer safeguards (SCCs or equivalent) are available to contracting customers on request."

I've attached a very short 'legal note' (one paragraph) that Susan can share with Acme's counsel if they ask for slightly more formal language. But I recommend we keep the public blurb short and link to the subprocessor list + DPA.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
